goal: Derive the first potentially nonzero short-time Taylor coefficient of the retarded source-to-Weyl Green response for the original AeST E' force in a smooth fixed Newtonian scalar approximation branch; explicitly flag what a leading coefficient does NOT prove.
assumptions: Fixed k>0, smooth original eta=0 FLRW background and consistent initial state
The local state-space linearization and original Einstein constraints hold, with no approximation-regime switch across the infinitesimal time interval
AeST effective fluid has no directly induced anisotropic shear from E at this order
Other species' shear perturbations and their first two temporal source derivatives have no direct E coefficient at the same instant, as expected from the exact Newtonian-gauge Einstein+AeST code
Q, a, rho_A, w_A, K_B and c_a² are finite, rho_A>0, 1+w_A>0, K_B>0; to conclude nonzero, require c_a²>0
Unit delta impulse in external F_E is a mathematical linear-system probe, NOT an admissible physical perturbation of X or bath history
Normalizations use CLASS conformal time and its total-fluid stress conventions, not a physical-lensing eta amplitude

exact_algebra.W_impulse_leading_term: G_WE(t,s)=(1/4)c_a²(s) K_B k² (t-s)²+o((t-s)²), provided shear's direct E short-time jet through this order vanishes
exact_algebra.caution: This is only the local nonzero Taylor jet of a mathematically independent external F_E->W control transfer. It is not the actual global Green solution and no physical X-history pair has been certified.

stop: If any direct instantaneous E->other-species shear terms, additional metric source terms, or approximation-specific constraint structure invalidate the Taylor jet, publish only the conditional algebra and DO NOT assert nonzero physical Green. Even a positive local jet does not establish full nonlinear action Ward closure or astronomical detection.
